races.name: By Chen Presidential Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Clementines Star
runners_data.note: Consistent placer in form (33-32) stepping back up to 7f where her best run came, jockey William Carver provides a yard-level booking for Kubler; the STYLE_FIT tag (prominent type mapped to a lead role) is less of a concern in a three-runner field where she simply inherits the front, and her good-ground form (1 place from 1 run) is at least mildly encouraging despite going unknown.

runners_data.name: Dolo's Star
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator with De Sousa in the saddle — a major positive in a race where timing off a slow pace matters — but her best placing has come over 5-6f and the step up to 7f on unknown going introduces a genuine stamina query; no wins from four starts and no placing on good ground make this a tough assignment despite the booking.

runners_data.name: Princess Honey Bee
runners_data.note: Returning after a 325-day absence, which is the single biggest question mark here, though her form figures include a third at 7f on good ground and she handles this trip in principle; Craig Lidster's 0 from 10 in the last 14 days is a flat trainer stat, and this long layoff means fitness cannot be assumed.

races.paceDynamic: Clementines Star is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner maiden, and with no other horse inclined to press from the front, she will dictate terms at whatever tempo she chooses across the seven furlongs at Thirsk. Both Dolo's Star and Princess Honey Bee are hold-up types, meaning the gallop will almost certainly be steady to moderate, with Clementines Star able to control every yard of the race without resistance. That uncontested lead, combined with a small field, means the front runner can conserve energy, dictate the pace of any stretch run, and make life genuinely difficult for horses needing a strong pace to bring them into contention late. This race shape heavily favours a prominent or front-running profile, and specifically rewards any horse that can travel smoothly in the slipstream or overtake a controlled pace-setter — the two closers will need either a misjudgement from Clementines Star or an unexpected injection of pace to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Wins Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Clementines Star settles into an uncontested lead and controls the tempo throughout, no pressure forcing her to burn early.
scenarios.body: She dictates a steady gallop, turns for home with a full tank, and the hold-up pair are left needing a sprint they have had no pace to aim at; a front-runner who controls the race in a three-runner field is extremely hard to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Catch Late
scenarios.trigger: If Clementines Star overcooks the early tempo or fades sharply in the final furlong, leaving a gap for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: One or both of Dolo's Star and Princess Honey Bee, sitting a length or two off the pace, find a sprint in the closing stages that the leader cannot match; a stumble in the final furlong or over-confidence from the rider would be necessary to trigger this outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Quickens Past
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops a strong enough mid-race pace to stretch Clementines Star, enabling a hold-up runner to arrive with a decisive late burst.
scenarios.body: Princess Honey Bee, with 7f form on good ground in her history, is the most likely candidate to pick up if the fractions have been honest; Dolo's Star has shown ability to finish second from off the pace but has no win from this profile yet.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so slow that the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole and all three runners are in contention at the same time.
scenarios.body: In a crawl-then-sprint scenario the horse with the best turn of foot benefits, but the going is unknown and a truly collapsed pace is rare even in small maiden fields; this is the least structured outcome and the hardest to predict.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Clementines Star is ridden positively from the gates — any hesitation and the pace vacuum in a three-runner field could create an awkward tactical battle with no horse willing to go forward.
Princess Honey Bee's 325-day absence is a serious fitness flag; monitor paddock behaviour and early market movement as a sharp drift could confirm she is not fully wound up.

Dolo's Star is unproven beyond 6f and has no placing on good ground — if Silvestre De Sousa is seen niggling for position in the first two furlongs, the step up in trip may be exposing a stamina limit.

With only three runners and both closers likely to track closely, Clementines Star's rider should be aware that even a modest pace advantage at the two-furlong pole could be enough to steal the race if the hold-up pair fail to accelerate quickly.

Going reported as unknown at Thirsk across all races — any late going-stick reading or clerk-of-the-course update before post time should be prioritised, particularly for Princess Honey Bee who has soft-ground form on her card.

races.name: Best Ticket Deals Online @Thirskraces Book Now Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Britain
runners_data.note: Two wins over 8f on Good ground in recent form and an excellent similar-going record (5/6 including 2W3P) make her the standout hold-up threat; apprentice Kyle McHugh (7lb) helps at the weights, but 308 days off the track is a significant query against fresh rivals.|

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Front-runner with a strong similar-going record (8/10) and a recent second at this trip on Good ground; the sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, so should get an uncontested lead, though it is technically a prominent runner placed here and a 5lb claim from Whiteley is a useful aid.|

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: A flagged tendency to fade in the finish is a serious concern in any shape that asks for a sustained effort; recent form figures (3-9-9-0) are poor and neither of its two stable-ground runs at Thirsk-relevant conditions inspire confidence, with headgear noted but not a clear improver flag.|

runners_data.name: Leelawadee
runners_data.note: In-form trainer Michael Dods sends this filly (4/28 over 14 days) into a small field where its natural deep hold-up position is harder to achieve — it is a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the race shape, and with only three career runs and no wins or places, it enters as the least exposed but also the least proven runner.|

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's operation is in fine form (7/73) and Hatamoto arrives on a short turnaround (13 days) having won over this exact trip and surface (1/8f/GOO); it will likely track Sandy Craic throughout and is the primary danger to the leader if it can sustain its effort to the line — headgear noted.|

races.paceDynamic: Sandy Craic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the off on Good ground at Thirsk over one mile. Hatamoto is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track Sandy Craic in second, meaning the pace is set by a single horse at whatever tempo suits connections — likely honest but not extreme. Lady Britain and Leelawadee are hold-up types, though Leelawadee has been redistributed to midfield because in a field this small the genuine hold-up positions are crowded; Leelawadee is unlikely to get as far back as natural, and its chance in a shape requiring a late run is discounted accordingly. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader on Good turf over a mile — strongly favours hold-up horses with a sustained finishing run or prominent types who can track the leader and pounce entering the final two furlongs, provided the pace is honest enough to set the race up for those coming from off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sandy Craic Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and the field never applies serious pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Sandy Craic bowls along in front with Hatamoto tracking at a respectful distance, the tempo controlled throughout and no rival willing or able to challenge the leader before the straight; when the field quickens entering the final two furlongs Sandy Craic's lead is already enough to hold on. Prominent types who have tracked efficiently without wasting energy benefit here, and Sandy Craic's recent second on Good ground and excellent similar-going record make this scenario the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic sets a genuinely honest gallop and the straight provides enough of a stamina test to reward those held up.
scenarios.body: Lady Britain, with two wins over this trip on Good ground in her recent history and the best similar-going profile in the race, comes from the rear to catch a tiring leader inside the final furlong; her strong form figures over 8f on Good (1-1) make her the prime candidate for this shape. Scheffler is less suited given its noted tendency to fade in the finish, meaning Lady Britain is the lone credible threat from the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closer Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Sandy Craic overcooks the tempo early and ties up in the final furlong, gifting the race to hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically strong early fractions from Sandy Craic leaves it vulnerable in the closing stages, and Lady Britain or a repositioned Leelawadee finds a clear passage on the outside to run past the weakening leader. Leelawadee's redistribution note means its chance here is partially discounted — it may not get as far back as needed — but Lady Britain, a genuine hold-up type, is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Hatamoto Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uneven or fractionally slow and Hatamoto, tracking the leader throughout, produces the sharpest turn of foot at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With a recent win over 8f on Good ground and multiple placed efforts at the trip, Hatamoto is best placed of the prominent runners to capitalise if Sandy Craic flattens out and no closer gets to them in time. This is the least likely shape given Sandy Craic's consistency, but Hatamoto's form figures and trainer Tim Easterby's strong 14-day record (7/73) make it a genuine if narrow alternative.

watchPoints.text: Sandy Craic's uncontested lead is the race's pivotal factor — if it bowls along undisturbed from the front, watch whether Hatamoto can close the gap entering the final two furlongs or whether the leader simply extends.|

Lady Britain's 308-day absence is a significant unknown; watch the market moves pre-race and her early positioning in running — if she misses the break or is blocked for a run, her chance evaporates in a five-runner field with limited room.|

Leelawadee cannot get its true deep hold-up berth in a five-runner race — watch whether Rhys Elliott (3lb) pushes forward from the gate, which would change its shape entirely and potentially alter the pace picture behind Sandy Craic.|

Scheffler's fade flag means watch it closely at the two-furlong marker — if it has worked its way into contention mid-race and then ties up, it could provide the gaps that other closers need to find a clear run.|

With the going listed as unknown despite Good conditions, watch for any firmness in the ground affecting stride patterns early — Sandy Craic and Lady Britain both have strong Good-ground profiles, but any quick break in the turf could play into Hatamoto's consistent placed form.|

races.name: Sell Your Business With Anderson Barrowcliff Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on soft previously but sim-going record here reads poorly (0W0P from 3 runs); a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is the rear, though the abundance of closers in this field means she is likely to find herself a little closer to the pace than ideal — that may not flatter her style.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby juvenile form at Thirsk is respectable but this horse's sim-going record over 5f on good is modest (1W2P from 11 runs); races from off the pace naturally but with so many hold-up types in the field she may be forced to bowl along in a midfield cluster rather than finding the clean air at the back she prefers.

runners_data.name: Davorge Nation
runners_data.note: A narrow winner over 5f on good ground last time out with Declan Carroll having just 1 from 8 in the last 14 days; the natural inclination is to drop out and come late, but with the field stacked with rear-trackers she will be jostling for position in a congested midfield and will need cleaner racing room than her style usually demands.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's 3yo has strong place form on good ground (2W4P from 9 sim-going runs) and races prominently with a high head carriage (hg:p noted); best placed to capitalise on an uncontested Empress Olivia lead by pressing from second and quickening off the bend, making this the most obvious position to benefit from the controlled pace shape.

runners_data.name: Houndhill
runners_data.note: Won last time out at Southwell on standard ground so the step back to turf on good is worth noting; races as a natural hold-up horse and while the redistribution effect may push her forward in the field, her best form (1 win, recent at Southwell) raises questions about whether she replicates that on a fast surface.

runners_data.name: Vinciamo
runners_data.note: Owns good place form over 5f on good ground (3 places from 6 sim-going runs) and is noted as wearing a tongue-tie (hg:t); Tom Eaves rides and this horse is a genuine hold-up performer by nature, though given the field profile he is among the most likely to claim a handy tracking berth just in behind the leaders rather than racing from the rear.

runners_data.name: Straight Ahead
runners_data.note: Two wins at Southwell on standard and a recent 4th at Carlisle on good suggest versatility, but his sim-going record on good turf reads 0W2P from 6 runs; Clifford Lee rides for Craig Lidster who has 0 from 10 in the last 14 days — worth noting the trainer's cold spell even if the horse's tactical profile (naturally hold-up) suits a patient ride from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 3yo has form placing on good ground (1W2P from 13 runs) and James Sullivan takes the ride; races from off the pace and has the profile of a horse who benefits from pace to chase, so the modest gallop set by a lone front-runner is a mild concern — she will need to quicken sharply from a crowded midfield group.

runners_data.name: Empress Olivia
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, she will likely bowl along in isolation without a challenger for the lead; her sim-going record on good turf (1W2P from 11 runs) is decent but her last two runs have been modest (0 and 4th), and while her tactical position is the most straightforward, STYLE_FIT notes she is technically mapped as prominent — the uncontested lead may slightly flatter her.

races.paceDynamic: Empress Olivia is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner 5f handicap at Thirsk and should secure an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable gallop without any serious challenger disputing for the early position. Simba's Pride is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely tuck in just behind, meaning the pace is controlled rather than searching. The bulk of this field — Yellow Diamonds, Under The Radar, Davorge Nation, Vinciamo, Straight Ahead, Angel Numbers and Houndhill — are natural hold-up or rear-tracking types, meaning closers will face a long, unobstructed passage but must still make up ground on a horse who has had an easy lead. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine straight-line speed who can close on a soft-gallop leader, and on a flat, sharp 5f track like Thirsk the premium is on those who can quicken efficiently from just off the pace rather than from deep in the field. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically race at the back, and of those pushed into midfield on the map, Vinciamo and Straight Ahead — who carry track-relevant form — are most likely to actually secure a handy tracking position closest to Empress Olivia.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Olivia Controls, Closers Chased
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia bowls along in front uncontested and the hold-up horses must come from off a modest pace set by a single front-runner.
scenarios.body: Empress Olivia dictates on her own terms and sets a tempo that neither exhausts the leaders nor frees up enough for the closers to close stylishly; horses who can track within three lengths and quicken will have the edge over deep hold-up types who need pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Blitz From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If Empress Olivia's pace is slower than expected and the closers generate enough momentum to sweep past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A very steady early pace ironically hands the advantage to the horse with the most raw speed off a slow tempo, allowing genuine hold-up performers to motor through on the outside.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Simba's Pride presses Empress Olivia hard enough to inject real pace and the two lead horses quicken clear before the hold-up runners can respond.
scenarios.body: Elevated early fractions compress the closing window and leave rear-trackers with too much ground to make up in the final 100 yards of a flat 5f track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uneven, the field bunches on the turn-in and a horse sitting mid-division in a compact group delivers a late burst through gaps.
scenarios.body: A messy middle-race dynamic suits a horse that has tracked smoothly without being forced wide or into traffic; redistribution concerns make this the least predictable shape.

watchPoints.text: Simba's Pride sits in the optimal tactical position for this race shape — prominent behind a sole uncontested leader on a flat 5f track — and his record of 2W4P on good ground marks him as the horse most structurally suited to how this race will be run.

Empress Olivia has the lead to herself but her last two runs have been poor (0 and 4th), and if she loses concentration or fails to quicken in the straight, the hold-up horses in the chasing pack will quickly close her down.

Vinciamo and Straight Ahead are the two redistributed hold-up types most likely to claim a forward-tracking berth; if both push up to race prominently behind Empress Olivia, the trio could create a compressed front group that squeezes Simba's Pride for racing room.

The going is officially unknown at Thirsk today — any significant overnight rain or unexpected watering that softens the surface would most benefit Yellow Diamonds and Davorge Nation, who both have winning form on soft, while potentially inconveniencing Simba's Pride whose form is built entirely on good ground.

Trainer cold spells: Craig Lidster (0/10, 14 days) and Mark Walford (0/14, 14 days) are both winless recently — if the market latches onto this in early trading, it may compress prices on the horses from more in-form yards such as Michael Dods (4/28) and Tim Easterby (7/73).

races.name: Don't Miss Summer Family Days @thirskraces Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and therefore the most influential horse in the race; Good going is fine but form away from this prominent role is unconvincing, and seven of eight career runs have been at shorter than a mile — stamina for the trip is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Bridgefoot Rambler
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer shunted forward on the map through redistribution — in truth this horse will try to settle last or near last; blinkered, trainer at 0/1 in the 14-day window, and five furlongs further than recent starts suggest stamina is the core question.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with multiple top-three finishes on Good going over this exact trip, giving her the most course-and-distance relevant profile in the field; not flashy but tidy, and Mark Winn rides a horse who knows the job.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who wears a hood and has a striking record at this distance on Good going, placing twice from five attempts at the trip; Ruth Carr's yard is in fair recent form and Taryn Langley's claim helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Create
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon has two winners from 12 in the past fortnight and this six-year-old has a placing at 8f on soft; however the horse's best form comes from a genuine hold-up position — squeezed forward by the redistribution, this is not ideal race shape for Create.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler has three winners from 23 in the 14-day window and Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a genuine asset; I Can Boogy has genuine front-rank intent and with a win and place from 15 runners on Good going is effective on this surface.

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: The in-form runner in the race — four winners from 28 in 14 days for Dods, won here over this trip on Good going (1/8f/GOO in recent hist), and the hood and tongue-tie are established; 11 days since last run is very fresh and the course record makes this one of the most relevant profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides a confirmed hold-up specialist mapped to midfield by necessity — this horse has four places from 15 outings on Good going and is consistent without winning; the 8-day turnaround is brisk and the natural racing position will be harder to find in this traffic.

runners_data.name: Here Comes Louie
runners_data.note: The fade-in-finish flag is a red light at a mile — this young three-year-old has posted unplaced efforts at similar trips and the redistribution away from a true hold-up position makes the challenge steeper; Roger Fell's yard is quiet (0/13 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Park Lane Penny
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves rides a three-year-old with a recent second over this exact course and distance (2/8f/GOO), giving Park Lane Penny strong positional form; Ivan Furtado has one winner from 27 runners in 14 days, modest strike rate, but the horse's own record here is the angle.

runners_data.name: Queenies Pal
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner moved forward on paper through redistribution — form on Good going is thin (2/8 runners placed) and the step up to a mile from recent seven-furlong outings is untested; the tongue-tie is worn but no trainer strike-rate support.

runners_data.name: Regal Knight
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is the most credentialled jockey in the field and this three-year-old has placed at eight and ten furlongs on Good going; a genuine hold-up performer, the redistribution forward is a concession, but De Sousa's ability to find a position from any draw is a mitigating factor.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Wore a visor in her last win over this trip on Good going (1/8f/GOO) and has the most directly relevant winning profile in the race; a front-prominent racer who should travel close to Aspire To Glory, she and Langholm are the two horses whose natural position and course record align most cleanly with the expected race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Aspire To Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — I Can Boogy and Trucial Pearl will press into prominent positions but neither is wired to go toe-to-toe for the front, meaning Aspire To Glory can control tempo from the outset at a pace of their own choosing. With a sustainable, uncontested lead over one mile on Good turf at Thirsk, the shape strongly favours horses close enough to track the leader without burning energy and who possess a finishing kick from a handy position. The field is saturated with true hold-up horses — Bridgefoot Rambler, Create, Without Delay, Here Comes Louie, Queenies Pal and Regal Knight are all genuine rear-division types redistributed into midfield on the map because they cannot all settle in their natural position — with the prominent slots most likely claimed by I Can Boogy, Trucial Pearl and Langholm. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can travel prominently or in the first half of the field, track a controlled pace, and produce a strong finish through the final two furlongs are overwhelmingly favoured; deep closers are structurally compromised by the uncontested tempo and will need an unusually strong gallop to get into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aspire To Glory Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Aspire To Glory settles into an uncontested lead at a measured gallop and none of the prominent runners apply sustained pressure through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: Aspire To Glory dictates on their own terms, the pace stays honest but not brutal, and horses tracking close behind have first call on the prize as the field strings out; a prominent racer with a late kick benefits enormously from saving energy across the first six furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to expose Aspire To Glory late, allowing a horse travelling in the first quarter to quicken past them inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Trucial Pearl or Langholm, nestled just off the pace and relaxed through the bend, arrives with a clean passage and overpowers a tiring leader; the one-mile trip at Thirsk suits a horse that settles and builds momentum from three furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If I Can Boogy and Trucial Pearl push Aspire To Glory into a faster-than-anticipated gallop, creating a stronger pace that opens the race up for horses arriving from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed from the rear who manage to find a forward enough position — Regal Knight or Without Delay — could get a tow into the race if the leaders burn each other out; however, with most closers forced wide of their natural role this scenario is materially discounted by the crowded hold-up section.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If a slow or variable early pace causes the field to bunch in the straight, creating a scrimmage that produces a surprising result from a horse who finds clear running by luck.
scenarios.body: In a race where ten horses are drawn from the same hold-up profile and all want similar ground through the final two furlongs, a traffic jam is possible — a horse like Park Lane Penny or Can I Kiss You who gets a clear early passage could capitalise on the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Langholm: won at this course over this trip on Good going and Michael Dods has four winners from 28 in 14 days — the combination of course form and trainer momentum makes this the most dangerous horse to the leader.

Trucial Pearl: the visor-wearing three-year-old won over this exact course, distance and going — she will travel prominently alongside Aspire To Glory and is the most likely horse to pounce late if the front-runner ties up.

Redistribution cluster — Bridgefoot Rambler, Create, Without Delay, Here Comes Louie, Queenies Pal and Regal Knight all want to race at the rear but cannot all do so; watch for traffic congestion in the home straight if the field bunches late.

Copper And Five: the ten-year-old holds strong place form at this trip on Good going and Taryn Langley's claim is notable — if the pace is truly sedate, veteran hold-up types with proven stamina could land from an unexpected position.

Aspire To Glory: sole confirmed front-runner, but has only one win from 15 starts on similar going and ran over shorter distances in most recent outings — if the mile proves a stretch, the race could open up for prominent trackers from two furlongs out.

races.name: Meijer Celebration Cup Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's former handler Declan Carroll holds this 4yo at OR 55 and has a modest 1/8 in the 14-day window; best recent form is a 3rd and 2nd at 6f on Good/Soft, making the step to 7f a slight query, but the Good going suits and 31 days fresh could sharpen him for a race with no pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr runner for James Sullivan who has been knocking consistently on the door — four places from his last ten on Good ground and twice placed at this exact 7f/Good combination makes him the most course-and-distance-relevant horse in the field; genuine hold-up style fits naturally into a sprint finish and he is one of the few not displaced from his role.|

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a win and five places on similar going, but his true style is deep hold-up and he has been pushed into the midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed — expect him to be further back than the map suggests, which in a no-pace race is a significant disadvantage; Tristan Davidson sends him here fresh off just 8 days.|

runners_data.name: Fair Isle Sioux
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners this 6yo who has only three runs on record and none better than fifth; naturally a hold-up horse but shown here in midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning he will likely race in a position that doesn't suit — limited form evidence on similar going compounds the concern.|

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason aboard this 4yo who has been knocking around in 6-7f handicaps all season without troubling the judge — five runs this season, best finish a pair of fourths, and the STA runs on Tapeta mean the Good turf form reads poorly; placed artificially into the midfield map but will likely drift further back given his natural inclinations.|

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Kevin & Lauren Frost who won over 6f on Standard and was placed over 5f on the same surface — the turf form is less convincing with a 6th and 10th on Good, and stepping to 7f for only the third time adds uncertainty; holds a natural hold-up tendency but may find himself up with the pace by default in this no-pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 5yo carries a hood (hg:p) and has placed three times from eight runs on similar going including a recent 3rd at 8f and 2nd at 7f on Good — genuinely suited by this trip and going combination but is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield position on the map; the quality of the placing run over 7f on Good is the most relevant data point.|

runners_data.name: Forever Twenty
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 3yo wears a tongue tie and has placed twice from eight runs on similar going, including a 3rd over 7f on Good; Alex Jary takes the 3lb claim which helps at the weights, but this is a genuine rear-of-field operator shown in midfield purely because the hold-up division is oversubscribed, and finding clear running in a bunched finish could be the decisive factor.|

runners_data.name: Crown Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is an obvious class upgrade in the saddle for this Ivan Furtado 3yo, but the horse has only three runs total — 10th, 4th, and 6th — and is unproven on 7f turf in a competitive handicap; a true hold-up runner by design, the redistribution to midfield means De Sousa's tactical awareness becomes the only edge.|

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's 3yo wears a tongue tie and has failed to trouble the judge in any of five starts, all finishes in the bottom half — the 0/3 trainer 14-day record adds no encouragement and 38 days off is the longest absence in the field; a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield, but the form simply doesn't suggest competitiveness in this grade.|

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this field carrying a hold-up style tag, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to impose a genuine gallop from the outset — this 7f contest at Thirsk is set to drift into a moderately-paced affair before developing into a mass sprint finish in the final two furlongs. The pace vacuum means the field will bunch and shuffle early, with nobody willing to commit, leaving the race shape entirely dependent on who gets first run from a compressed pack. Emerald Army, Captain Cess, and Elashgar are the least hold-up-dependent of the group and may find themselves pushed closer to the front by circumstance rather than design. Coconut Bay, Fair Isle Sioux, Night Emperor, Misemerald, Forever Twenty, Crown Of Dreams, and Breeze Star are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the race is oversubscribed — they are unlikely to find their natural position and several will be racing out of role entirely. The tactical verdict is clear: in a sprint-finish handicap with no pace, the horse that gets the clearest run through a congested pack and quickens best from a handy position wins — runners with strong recent form on Good ground over 7f and a jockey capable of reading the muddled gallop early hold the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Bunch
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and detonates into a wall-to-wall sprint from the two-furlong pole, with no horse able to dominate
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of raw acceleration from a tight, compressed group, rewarding any runner that gets a clear passage and can sustain a strong finishing effort over the final quarter-mile; horses with proven closing speed on Good turf over this trip are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners drift to the front by default and set a modest honest pace that suits those racing closest to the action
scenarios.body: A gentle gallop allows any runner that settles just off the non-pace to dictate into the straight without burning energy, leaving them with enough in reserve to hold on; Captain Cess and Elashgar, who have both shown ability to race closer than their style tag implies, benefit most from this accidental lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If one runner goes genuinely hard from the front creating a true test of stamina and the field strings out
scenarios.body: A fast early pace over 7f on Good turf would set up a strong late run from the deepest hold-up types, but the critical caveat is that most of those runners are redistributed and unlikely to be far enough back to produce a genuine late surge; even so, Misemerald and Crown Of Dreams have the profile to benefit if the shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Finish No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the field races in a tight traffic-ridden bunch throughout with multiple horses meeting interference in the straight
scenarios.body: No horse gets a clean run and the race is decided on luck and position rather than merit, with a short-priced hold-up type finding a gap at the last moment; any runner that has a clear draw advantage or a jockey experienced at Thirsk in these conditions gains disproportionate influence.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army — the only runner with multiple placed efforts at this exact trip and going combination (7f/Good) without redistribution from role; if he gets a clear run in the sprint finish he is the most structurally suited horse in the race.

Coconut Bay — despite a 8-day turnaround and redistribution out of his natural position, he holds the lone win on similar going in this field; watch whether Jason Hart attempts to manufacture a forward position or accepts a wider disadvantage.

Crown Of Dreams — Silvestre De Sousa on a 3yo with only three career runs and no win creates a significant information gap; De Sousa may try to manufacture an unexpected position and could produce something out of nothing in a muddled no-pace race.

Misemerald — the hood and recent placed efforts over 7f on Good are the most directly relevant recent form in the race; watch whether Clifford Lee can find daylight through what will be a very congested final two furlongs.

Forever Twenty — the 3lb claim for Alex Jary is meaningful at these low weights in a tight handicap, and Furtado has both this horse and Crown Of Dreams declared, which raises tactical questions about which stable runner is the preferred runner.

races.name: Thirsk Sky Bet Summer Festival Day Friday 24th July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: Form includes a recent second on good ground over this exact 8f trip and the O'Meara yard is in reasonable nick; a genuine hold-up type whose best chance requires a genuinely strong pace that this small field of six looks unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: Barron yard has been quiet (0/8 in 14 days) and William Pyle takes over in the saddle; races from the rear on good ground where it has shown placed form, but like Capital Guarantee it needs genuine tempo to be produced to its best effect.

runners_data.name: Harswell Ruby
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides and Roger Fell's filly has headgear on (hood in today's card), finishing second over this exact 8f on good ground recently; races prominently by nature and that profile sits attractively in this shape behind an uncontested leader.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the ride for Phillip Makin and this horse is the confirmed pace-setter, having won over 8f on good ground; it has 34 days between runs which is worth monitoring, but the uncontested lead is a clear tactical asset and the style fit score reflects it races slightly outside its optimal position band — in practice, it simply leads here.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: O'Meara's eight-year-old is a true prominent racer by inclination, but with Military Leader and Harswell Ruby ahead of it in the pecking order for the front positions, it is unlikely to secure its natural pitch and the style-fit discount is meaningful; form has been modest this season (0-9576) and age may be catching up.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has a solid placed record on good ground over this trip (three places from five recent runs) and wears a hood; a genuine hold-up horse at heart, it cannot get as far forward as it might like in this field, so the redistribution nudges it into a midfield position that is not truly its own — treat its chance in prominent-pace scenarios accordingly.

races.paceDynamic: Military Leader is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the off — a sustainable tempo rather than a scorching one over a mile on good ground at Thirsk. Harswell Ruby will look to press or sit just off the leader in second position, meaning the front two set a comfortable framing pace that may not fully stretch the hold-up horses until late. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all naturally hold their position: Military Leader is best placed to secure the lead, with Cosmos Raj — a genuine prominent racer by nature — likely to be frustrated back into midfield, and Barley similarly unable to get as far forward as it would ideally like. A sustainable, uncontested lead favours the prominent/press profile — specifically anything racing close to Military Leader in second or third — as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring genuine closers off a true strong pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Military Leader Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Military Leader leads uncontested and dictates a comfortable gallop, opponents cannot pick up early enough.
scenarios.body: Military Leader sets a sustainable tempo from flag to finish, and the runner who travels closest in Harswell Ruby's position is best placed to pounce in the straight with something in reserve. Hold-up horses Capital Guarantee and Degale will need a stronger gallop than this shape is likely to generate to close the gap effectively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Press Horse Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Harswell Ruby pushes Military Leader harder than expected and the tempo lifts sufficiently to expose the leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Harswell Ruby tracks Military Leader aggressively, and if the leader's stamina is tested, a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace stands to benefit most. Cosmos Raj, if able to force a natural prominent position despite the redistribution pressure, could emerge as a factor here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and hold-up horses get a strong enough sectional to close from behind.
scenarios.body: Capital Guarantee and Degale, both genuine hold-up types on form, require a more searching gallop than this field of six seems likely to produce to make up ground in time. Even if the race does open up, both must overcome a tactical situation that has not been set up in their favour.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Flurry Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes muddled mid-race with horses reshuffling and the front two tire simultaneously.
scenarios.body: Barley, though its true style is hold-up and it is unlikely to get a forward pitch, could emerge if the field strings out unevenly and gaps appear late. Cosmos Raj, also denied its natural position, is the other candidate if the race dissolves into a scramble rather than a clean tactical shape.

watchPoints.text: Military Leader's 34-day absence means any sign of greenness or sluggishness at the start could immediately undermine the uncontested lead scenario and destabilise the entire pace map.

Cosmos Raj is a natural front-runner who will be squeezed for position at the break — watch whether it fights for prominence and increases the tempo unexpectedly, or settles for a compromised midfield pitch.

Harswell Ruby's hood (headgear flagged) and quick turnaround (9 days) makes its early behaviour critical — if it over-races pressing Military Leader it could turn a sedate gallop into a genuine test and transform the race shape.

With only six runners on good ground at Thirsk over a mile, watch whether the field becomes well strung out early — a wide, processional shape would benefit the front two and actively harm Capital Guarantee and Degale's chances of closing late.
